recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group wants to retire every remaining use of "literal identity" across the specification, handle that as a separate terminology-cleanup issue.
issue_request: FHIR-17105 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core BaseResource issue asking to define the then-used term "literal identity" and explain resource identity generally, not only as an HTTP server base plus resource type plus logical id.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn 14500, represented in git as 7ee661f6b4022414f36a63274872d7ef207a8716, which cites GF#17105 and rewrote the problematic resource identity paragraph from "literal identity"/"unique identifier" wording to "location" wording with added non-REST context guidance.
additional_context: Current source/resource/resource-notes.xml keeps the clarification and no longer uses "literal identity" in the resource.html#id section. Repository search finds the phrase only in source/managing.html, where the preceding paragraph defines resource identity as a URI/URL, and source/valueset/valueset-introduction.xml, where the phrase is parenthetically defined. FHIR-15615 and FHIR-14191 were co-applied in the same historical commit but have broader identifier/canonical URL scopes and were not separately decided.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active source already conveys the requested clarification; adding another definition or restating the guidance would be redundant and could create maintenance drift.
